In the exceptional case every maximizing P gives Π1Tr_B(XdP)Π2=Π1Tr_A(XdP)Π2=0. Hence ker D⊆ker J† for EVERY 16×2 isometry Ψ in the original Schur coupling reduction. same_sector: If matching scalar t≠0, rank≤2 forces one local traceless 2×2 block to vanish and the other have eigenvalues ±t; its chosen sector has exactly two equal top singular values κ²=||D||²+2|t|² and all other sectors strictly smaller. If t=0 and both C,D are nonzero, rank≤2 forces C²=D²=λ²I; simultaneous independent 2×2 Schur forms give two equal nonzero singular squares κ²=||C||²+||D||², strictly exceeding all other sector norms. If one C,D vanishes, rank≤2 forces the other rank-one, giving one zero factor exception.
same_row_column: Equality in each weighted lemma gives D_s=t_s(2P_s−I), C²=4t_s²I, hence t1²=t2² and αβ=0. If t_s≠0, each selected sector has exactly one top singular square ||C||²+8|t|²≥16|t|² while all other candidates are strictly smaller, including the opposite row whose norm²=4|t|². Thus gap. If t_s=0, both D_s=0, unused C block=0 and equality forces C rank-one; this is the one-zero-factor exception. Same column symmetric.
opposite: Opposite-row/column equality forces both factors normal; the independently written evaluation-Gram equality classification then gives σ2>σ3 for every nonzero saturated normal pair.
exception: If A is rank-one traceless and B=0, every maximizing P is |v⟩⟨v|⊗Q with rank(Q)=2, and A=σ|u⟩⟨v| has ⟨v,u⟩=0. Thus Tr_A(XdP)=0 and Tr_B(XdP)=2A, the latter block diagonal. The swapped case is analogous.
